resale_co.name: Certificate of Land Use Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: City of Brigantine Construction Office (Construction Official or designee; Land Use Administrator)
resale_co.lead_time: The City code says the Construction Official may inspect within five working days of the application and acts on a completed application within five working days (seen in search results of the code).
requirements: Application for Certificate of Land Use Compliance (owner, applicant, block and lot, present and proposed use)

Land Use Administrator review of zoning classification and permitted use (single family, townhouse, approved conditional or existing non-conforming use), open permits or violations (NOP/NOV) and flood zone
Possible inspection of the house by the Construction Official or designee
Smoke/CO alarm certificate from the Bureau of Fire Prevention (separate, see fire certificate)

fees.label: Certificate of Land Use Compliance (City fee ordinance)
Certificate of Land Use Compliance (application form)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application Certificate of Land Use Compliance (posted on the Construction Office page as 'Land Use Application rev.4.4.25') and file it with the $75.00 fee (check or cash) at the Construction Office, City Hall, 1417 West Brigantine Avenue, Brigantine, NJ 08203. Questions: (609) 266-7600 ext. 261 or construction@brigantinenj.gov. The certificate does not replace a building permit.

evidence.quote: PER CITY OF BRIGANTINE CHAPTER 134 A certificate of land use compliance shall be required prior to the sale or any other type of transfer of title of any structure in the City of Brigantine, including but not limited to any time-sharing unit.
APPLICATION CERTIFICATE OF LAND USE COMPLIANCE
**NOTE: THIS CERTIFICATE DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE FOR A BUILDING PERMIT

The Construction Official or his duly authorized designee shall have the authority to issue certificates of land use compliance, but only in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.

resale_co.notes: Changed from not_found: the form posted on the Construction Office page as 'Land Use Application rev.4.4.25' is the City's Application Certificate of Land Use Compliance. It quotes City Code Chapter 134: a certificate of land use compliance is required before the sale or any other transfer of title of any structure. The form is a scan (read by eye); the Chapter 134 text on ecode360 (https://ecode360.com/7165345, titled 'City of Brigantine, NJ: Certificate of Land Use Compliance') could only be seen through search results. Those results also say the Construction Official or designee may inspect within five working days of filing and must grant or deny a completed application within five working days, that a denial can be appealed to the Zoning Board within 10 working days, and that the certificate states the structure is an appropriate and allowable use. The $75.00 fee appears both on the form and in the City fee ordinance (Ordinance No. 24 of 2025, adopted December 3, 2025). The form header lists ext. 261 and construction@brigantinenj.gov; the Construction Office page lists ext. 260 and an email hidden behind email protection (decoded earlier as Construction@BrigantineBeachnj.com). Separately, the Construction Office's January 2024 UCC fee schedule lists 'Continued Certificate of Occupancy 300.00' among construction certificates; nothing says it applies to a home sale. Brigantine also has a rental registration and rental inspection program run by the Bureau of Fire Prevention; that is a rental program. The smoke/CO fees are repeated here because the City charges them through the same fee ordinance.

requirements: Request a Smoke Detector/CO (Sale) inspection; the form asks for number of bedrooms and bathrooms, heat, water heater and stove fuel, fireplace and garage
Property access for the inspector (key, lock box number or door code) and occupant contact if occupied

Portable fire extinguisher: at least one, listed and charged, 2A:10B:C to 10 lb, on the maker's hanger or bracket, within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, visible, near an exit path, with owner's manual (posted 2005 DCA memo)
Fire extinguisher must have the original sales receipt (note on the posted memo)

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Bureau of Fire Prevention Request for Inspection form, check 'Smoke Detector/CO (Sale)', and give the settlement date, realty office, agent contact, property details and access (key, lock box or door code). Send it by email to Fireprevention@brigantinebeachnj.com or fax 609-266-0291, or bring it to 1417 W Brigantine Avenue. The form records payment by check or cash.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA is the fire code enforcing agency (registry code S), and the DCA's July 2026 list of state towns marks Brigantine 'SC' (state smoke certificates). However, the City's own Bureau of Fire Prevention posts a Request for Inspection form with a 'Smoke Detector/CO (Sale)' option, the state fire directory lists Brigantine City at 1417 W Brigantine Av, (609) 266-3102, under smoke detector compliance, and the City's fee ordinance adopted December 3, 2025 sets the certificate fees, so the City bureau is recorded as the issuer. Confirm with the bureau whether the State portal is ever used instead. The same ordinance also has a second, conflicting entry under S ('6. Certificate of smoke detector carbon monoxide alarm and portable fire extinguisher compliance') with $35.00 / $70.00 / $125.00 for the same timing tiers; the $45 / $90 / $161 entry is recorded. The bureau's email is hidden behind an email-protection link on the page and decodes to fireprevention@brigantinebeachnj.com (the form prints Fireprevention@brigantinebeachnj.com). Staff listed: Barbara Deery, 609-266-7600 ext. 303, and Katie Lynn, ext. 310 (both bdeery@brigantinenj.gov after decoding), and Riley Lorenz, ext. 266, rlorenz@brigantinenj.gov. The page still posts a 2005 DCA memo requiring a fire extinguisher at resale; the state law of February 3, 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19) removed the extinguisher from the state requirement, and the City's fee ordinance still names it.

other_items.label: Water/sewer special reading for sale
other_items.detail: Request a special water reading with the Water Reading Request form (email taxcollector@brigantinebeachnj.com); allow 5 business days; $60.00 charge for a sale, collected at settlement by separate check. Quote: 'Based on Ordinance #20 pr 2022: there is a $60.00 charge for this special reading for the sale of a property.'

other_items.label: Lead service line proof (possible)
other_items.detail: Search results for the City code (Lead Service Line Replacement article, Ord. No. 23-2022) say that on the sale or transfer of a dwelling the owner must show the lead service line was replaced, or a completed right of entry form for the City's replacement program, to get a certificate of occupancy, certificate of land use compliance and smoke/CO certificates. Seen only in search results; confirm with the City.

open_questions: Confirm the Certificate of Land Use Compliance process for a 1-2 family sale: is an inspection always done, how long it takes, and how long the certificate stays valid?
Does the City require proof of lead service line replacement (or a right of entry form) before issuing the land use or smoke certificates at sale?
Which smoke/CO fee is current: $45 / $90 / $161 or the conflicting $35 / $70 / $125 entry in the same 2025 ordinance?
Does the Bureau of Fire Prevention always issue the resale smoke/CO certificate, or does the State DCA portal apply (the DCA list marks Brigantine 'SC')?
